questions.q: What does the Sales Director want this time, compared to the Beginner project's one-off pull?
options: Access to the raw AdventureWorks2012 database itself
A single static PDF emailed once
An executive summary that refreshes automatically every week
A report with no numbers, just narrative commentary
questions.explain: The Sales Director's ask is a recurring, auto-refreshing executive summary for the weekly leadership meeting, not another one-time pull.

questions.q: What does the Operations Manager need that the Sales Director doesn't?
options: The exact same executive summary page, just in a different color
A printed copy instead of a Power BI report
A page she can filter and slice by specific regions and product lines herself
A page with no filters at all
questions.explain: The Operations Manager's job is exploratory drill-down by region and product line, which is a different page design than a fixed executive summary.

questions.q: Why does a recurring, two-stakeholder report need a real data model with relationships, rather than one flat query result?
options: Two pages pulling different cuts of the same numbers need shared, related tables behind them, not one pasted-in result
Relationships are required by Power BI's licensing terms
It doesn't — a flat query result would work exactly as well
Flat query results can't be opened in Power BI at all
questions.explain: Different pages need different cuts of the same underlying facts, which is exactly what a modeled fact/dimension structure with relationships supports.

questions.q: Which real AdventureWorks2012 table holds one row per order LINE, including the product and quantity?
options: Sales.SalesOrderDetail
Sales.SalesOrderHeader
Production.ProductSubcategory
Sales.SalesTerritory
questions.explain: Sales.SalesOrderDetail is the line-item-grain table — one row per product per order, with quantity and line total.

questions.q: What does this chapter intentionally include that the Beginner project didn't?
options: A requirement to rebuild the entire report from scratch every day
A real bug where two pages show mismatched numbers, which gets diagnosed and fixed
A rule against ever using CALCULATE in DAX
A second, unrelated database with no connection to AdventureWorks2012
questions.explain: Lessons 10-12 walk through noticing, root-causing, and fixing a genuine DAX mismatch bug between the two report pages.
